title: Probabilistic DR decision engine and scheduled chaos exercises
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current active-passive failover playbooks are prescriptive and heavyweight. During recent partial-region degradations we observed either premature failovers or delayed promotions because decisions were manual and binary. We need a decision layer that makes probabilistic failover recommendations based on SLO telemetry, capacity headroom, and error-mode classification, paired with a deterministic, automated drill cadence (chaos + scheduled) that validates backups, restore fidelity, and recovery RTO/RPOs.

Goal: Build a DR Decision Engine (DDE) that ingests SLO signals, capacity/queue metrics, and circuit-breaker state to produce a ranked set of actions (wait, scale, route-shed, promote-standby, run-restore). Ship a safe automation path to execute non-destructive actions during drills and a manual-approval path for production evocations. Bake in backup/restore verification tasks into the drill flow so every scheduled drill validates snapshot integrity, incremental replay, and KV cache reconciliation.

Success criteria: 
- DDE recommendations align with postmortem-validated decisions in 90% of historical incidents (measured in simulation).
- Automated drills run monthly across 2 regions, completing backup/restore validation and reaching stated RTO <= 10 minutes for control-plane failover and RPO <= 5 minutes for tokenstore.
- No customer-facing errors during safe-mode drills (use traffic fencing/canary routing).
- Console shows per-drill audit trail: recommended action, executed action, metrics at time-of-decision, and reconciliation results.
acceptance_criteria: DDE simulator imported historical incidents and produces matching recommendations in >=90% of cases
A templated drill can be scheduled from Console with a single button press and runs end-to-end in a sandboxed mode
Backup/restore validation steps include checksum verification, incremental replay test, and application-level canary against read/write lanes
Circuit-breaker and load-shed policies are exercised in the drill and metrics recorded: trip thresholds, recovery time, and shed percentage
Runbook steps are documented and have one on-call and one secondary assigned for each scheduled drill
Security review and KMS access gating for restore operations completed and signed off
runbook_steps: Pre-drill: create drill ticket and announce to on-call rotation; snapshot current config and export SLO baselines
Sandbox deploy: provision isolated traffic fences and customer-simulation tenant(s) in target standby region
Telemetry gating: ensure synthetic SLO probes for latency, error-rate, and tail-latency streaming are active
DDE dry-run: ingest live telemetry and run recommendation engine in "dry" mode; capture recommended action and confidence score
Safe actions: run non-destructive actions (scale-up, route lighter-weight traffic, toggle canary routing) and validate observability
Backup snapshot validation: verify checksum and manifest for last full + incremental; fail the drill if integrity mismatch
Restore validation: execute incremental restore into sandbox, run end-to-end smoke tests, run KV reconciliation check (checksum + key-count diff within tolerance)
Canary promotion: simulate tokenstore promotion by flipping read/write proxies for sandbox tenant and verify writes are accepted and replayed to downstream indexes
Circuit-breaker exercise: inject two failure modes (growing backend error-rate; latency tail increase) and validate CB trips at configured thresholds and auto-unfreeze behavior
Load-shedding exercise: trigger shed policy for a heavy-tenant in sandbox, ensure drop rate metrics match configured policy, and verify graceful degradation responses from SDKs
Post-drill: capture execution logs, attach PR/Confluence artifacts, create follow-up issues for any failures, and schedule remediation
Production escalation path: only after green in sandbox; require explicit approval from SRE lead and product security to run any destructive production steps
Audit: push drill artifacts to Console audit stream and to corporate S3 bucket with encryption and retention policy
validation_checks: Snapshot checksum equality across primary and standby within 30s of snapshot completion
Incremental restore write-through verification: 100 writes accepted, 95% readable after replay
KV cache rehydrate time: median < 45s, p95 < 2m for active tenant workload
Tokenstore promotion end-to-end RTO <= 10 minutes in sandbox
RPO for message-queueed in-flight requests <= 5 minutes as measured by watermark lag
SLO probe success rate >= targeted baseline during drill: >= 99.95% for control-plane endpoints
Error budget burn delta recorded and compared to pre-drill baseline
drill_schedule: Monthly sandbox drill: first Wednesday of month, regions eu-west-1 <-> us-west-2 (non-overlapping business hours)
Quarterly full-failover dry-run: Saturday window; includes DNS cutover simulation and dependency fencing
Ad-hoc post-incident targeted drills: within 14 days of any production incident >P0
Onboarding drills: new infra or major runtime release must pass a successful sandbox drill before GA rollout
automation_tasks: Build DDE simulator ingest pipeline to replay historical telemetry (error rate, latency, queue depth) from last 24 months
Implement confidence-scoring model that weighs SLO burn, capacity headroom, and CB state to produce recommended action and TTL
Add Console UI to launch scheduled drills with parameterized regions and safe-mode flag
Create a reversible automation path for tokenstore promotion with explicit manual-confirm step in production
Extend observability to capture DDE inputs and decisions in a single timeline for auditability
Automate backup manifest verification and KV checksum reporters as part of CI for every backup job
Scripted post-restore smoke tests and application-level end-to-end verification harness
